horizon_finding.question: The coordinator asked whether the walk's depth limit binds, and said: if it does not, change nothing and say so.
horizon_finding.answer: IT BINDS, and the finding is larger than the wording. Sweep over depths 1..12 on the patched mirror: codes 5, 11, 12, 14, 16, 16 at depths 1-6, then 21 at depth 7 and 26 at depth 8+. So the population SATURATES at 16 codes by depth 5 and is unchanged at 6; at depth 7 the walk first admits codes whose consumer is not the login path at all - no_mail_client (contact.rs, opening a mail client) and connection_not_configured (messaging.rs) - and at depth 8 also the external_url_* and connection_change_requires_* families.
horizon_finding.what_this_means: My predicate does NOT measure reachability in the compiler's sense; it measures 'within N hops of call-name references'. Depth 6 produced the right answer, and before this sweep it was a TUNED parameter - a right answer for the wrong reason, which is the class we have been removing all day. I tried three times to make the walk semantic instead (follow only where the error propagates through `?`, then treating map_err field-projection as forwarding): each attempt was depth-independent but under-reached, missing both positive controls, because calls in closure-tail positions carry errors too. Rather than keep tuning privately I stopped and measured the structure.
horizon_finding.resolution: The horizon stays 6, but it is now a MEASURED boundary with both edges asserted in the harness, so the number cannot drift silently: a LOWER-edge control proves the population is already saturated at depth 5 (nothing new appears at 6), and an UPPER-edge control proves that at depth 7 the walk leaves the login path and admits unmapped codes - today it names exactly external_url_refused, external_url_unavailable, external_url_unsupported, no_mail_client. If either edge moves, the stage reddens. And the assert's NAME no longer overstates: it says 'within the MEASURED horizon (6 call-name hops, saturated at 5, contaminated at 7)', not 'every reachable code'.
horizon_finding.honest_limit: This is a name-hop horizon pinned by measurement, NOT a proof that no code outside it can reach the login command. A real propagation analysis needs closure-tail and trait-dispatch handling and is not in this slice. Stated so nobody reads the assert as stronger than it is.

streams.coverage_finding: Found by the coordinator against my own regex and adopted by the manager as decision (1707): the map yields 22 unique text-key targets while the hand-written list held 18, a strict subset. FOUR routable refusal codes had NO check whatsoever - migration_required, connection_expired, tenant_mismatch, ownership_conflict - and the absence was invisible only because their texts happen to exist. This is a COVERAGE fact, not a refactoring detail: replacing the hand-written list with a derived one is what brings those four under a check for the first time, and they are named in the handover as previously uncovered. The general rule (1707): a list enumerating the elements of a source is never typed by hand beside that source - it is derived from it, because a hand-written copy falls behind silently and the lag does not redden while side conditions happen to agree.
